verses.1: The rest, brothers and sisters, rejoice in the Lord. To write these things to you is not burdensome to me, but it is safe for you.
verses.2: Watch out for the dogs, watch out for the evil workers, watch out for the circumcision.
verses.3: For we are the circumcision, who worship God in the Spirit and glory in Christ Jesus and put no confidence in the flesh—
verses.4: even though I myself have confidence also in the flesh. If anyone else has a basis for confidence in the flesh, I have even more:
verses.5: circumcised on the eighth day, of the people of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of Hebrews, in regard to the law a Pharisee,
verses.6: in zeal a persecutor of the church, in righteousness under the law blameless.
verses.7: But whatever gains I had, I have counted as loss because of Christ.
verses.8: Moreover, I count everything as loss for the surpassing value of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord, for whose sake I have suffered the loss of all things and count them as dung, so that I may gain Christ
verses.9: and be found in him, not having a righteousness of my own based on the law, but one that is through faith in Christ—the righteousness that comes from God on the basis of faith,
verses.10: so that I may know him and the power of his resurrection and may share in his sufferings, becoming like him in his death,
verses.11: in order if possible to attain the resurrection from the dead.
verses.12: Not that I have already obtained this or have already been made perfect, but I press on to take hold of that for which I was also taken hold of by Christ Jesus.
verses.13: Brothers and sisters, I do not consider myself to have taken hold of it yet. One thing I do: forgetting what lies behind and reaching forward to what lies ahead,
verses.14: I press toward the goal for the prize of the heavenly calling of God in Christ Jesus.
verses.15: Therefore, as many as are mature, let this mind be in you. And if you think otherwise, this too God will reveal to you.
verses.16: But as for what we have already attained, let us walk by that same standard.
verses.17: Join with me in following my example, brothers and sisters, and observe those who live according to the model you have in us,
verses.18: for many live as enemies of the cross of Christ, of whom I have told you often and now say with weeping,
verses.19: whose end is destruction, whose god is their stomach, and whose glory is their shame, who set their minds on earthly things.
verses.20: For our citizenship is in heaven, from which we also eagerly await a Savior, the Lord Jesus Christ,
verses.21: who will transform our lowly body to be like his glorious body, according to the working of the power that enables him to subject all things to himself.

notes:
Notes
- v. 9: "σκύβαλα" is translated as "dung" to reflect the strong dismissive tone without archaizing the language.
- v. 19: "ὧν τὸ τέλος ἀπώλεια" is translated as "whose end is destruction" to reflect the final fate of those described.
- v. 19: "ὧν ὁ θεὸς ἡ κοιλία" is translated as "whose god is their stomach" to capture the metaphor of misplaced devotion.
- v. 21: "μετασχηματίσει" is rendered as "transform" to emphasize the radical change implied.
raw:
[1] The rest, brothers and sisters, rejoice in the Lord. To write these things to you is not burdensome to me, but it is safe for you.

[2] Watch out for the dogs, watch out for the evil workers, watch out for the circumcision.

[3] For we are the circumcision, who worship God in the Spirit and glory in Christ Jesus and put no confidence in the flesh—

[4] even though I myself have confidence also in the flesh. If anyone else has a basis for confidence in the flesh, I have even more:

[5] circumcised on the eighth day, of the people of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of Hebrews, in regard to the law a Pharisee,

[6] in zeal a persecutor of the church, in righteousness under the law blameless.

[7] But whatever gains I had, I have counted as loss because of Christ.

[8] Moreover, I count everything as loss for the surpassing value of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord, for whose sake I have suffered the loss of all things and count them as dung, so that I may gain Christ

[9] and be found in him, not having a righteousness of my own based on the law, but one that is through faith in Christ—the righteousness that comes from God on the basis of faith,

[10] so that I may know him and the power of his resurrection and may share in his sufferings, becoming like him in his death,

[11] in order if possible to attain the resurrection from the dead.

[12] Not that I have already obtained this or have already been made perfect, but I press on to take hold of that for which I was also taken hold of by Christ Jesus.

[13] Brothers and sisters, I do not consider myself to have taken hold of it yet. One thing I do: forgetting what lies behind and reaching forward to what lies ahead,

[14] I press toward the goal for the prize of the heavenly calling of God in Christ Jesus.

[15] Therefore, as many as are mature, let this mind be in you. And if you think otherwise, this too God will reveal to you.

[16] But as for what we have already attained, let us walk by that same standard.

[17] Join with me in following my example, brothers and sisters, and observe those who live according to the model you have in us,

[18] for many live as enemies of the cross of Christ, of whom I have told you often and now say with weeping,

[19] whose end is destruction, whose god is their stomach, and whose glory is their shame, who set their minds on earthly things.

[20] For our citizenship is in heaven, from which we also eagerly await a Savior, the Lord Jesus Christ,

[21] who will transform our lowly body to be like his glorious body, according to the working of the power that enables him to subject all things to himself.

---
Notes
- v. 9: "σκύβαλα" is translated as "dung" to reflect the strong dismissive tone without archaizing the language.
- v. 19: "ὧν τὸ τέλος ἀπώλεια" is translated as "whose end is destruction" to reflect the final fate of those described.
- v. 19: "ὧν ὁ θεὸς ἡ κοιλία" is translated as "whose god is their stomach" to capture the metaphor of misplaced devotion.
- v. 21: "μετασχηματίσει" is rendered as "transform" to emphasize the radical change implied.
